notSupported: instancing a whole node hierarchy of a glTF asset

rules: Declarations, fields, assignments and statements end with ';', also the last one before '}'.
Float literals have digits on both sides of the point (1.0, 0.5, 2.5e-3), never 1. or .5; integer literals have no sign, no leading zeros and no hexadecimal form.
Comparison operators (< <= > >=) and equality operators (== !=) do not chain: write (a < b) && (b < c).
Typed values are never converted implicitly: an i32 value is not an f32 value, and only a literal such as 1 may stand where an f32 is expected.
An import is import { Name } from "./path.mtek"; the path is relative (starts with ./ or ../) and ends in .mtek.
Every scene needs a camera: camera Main { position: vec3(0.0, 2.0, 5.0); }.
Fields and parameters must exist on their schema or declaration: an unknown name is an error, never ignored.

schemaGuide: A field line reads `name: type = default [flags] range R // meaning`. Flags: R required, W writable from handlers, B bindable with bind(..), C construction-only (a constant expression). A field that is not listed does not exist. Function [brackets] mark optional arguments; [handler] means handlers/lifecycle only.

schemas.name: Box
schemas.doc: An axis-aligned box centred on the origin.
fields: size: vec3 = vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) [C] // Full extents along X, Y and Z.

schemas.name: BoxCollider
fields: size: vec3 [RC] // Full extents along X, Y and Z.
sensor: bool = false [C] // A sensor reports collisions but does not push other bodies.
friction: f32 = 0.5 [C] // Coulomb friction coefficient.
restitution: f32 = 0.0 [C] range 0…1 // Bounciness, 0 (none) to 1 (perfect).

schemas.name: Camera
schemas.doc: The fields of a `camera` scene object. Looks along its local -Z axis, or at `target` when one is declared.
fields: position: vec3 = vec3(0.0, 0.0, 5.0) [WB] // Camera position in world space, in metres.
target: vec3 [WB] // Optional point to look at (up is +Y). When declared, `rotation` must not be.
rotation: quat = quat.identity() [WB] // Orientation when no `target` is declared.
projection: projection = Perspective {} [C] // `Perspective {..}` or `Orthographic {..}`. The projection kind is construction-only; the fields of the descriptor are writable and bindable.
active: bool [C] // Marks the active camera. Optional when the scene has exactly one camera; with several cameras exactly one must declare `active: true`.

exposure: f32 = -1.9145305 [C] // Exposure value EV100; lit materials are scaled by 1 / (1.2 * 2^exposure). The default, -log2(1.2 * pi), shows a white Lambertian surface under a 1 lux light as white; a sunny day (about 100 000 lux) is about 15.

schemas.name: DirectionalLight
schemas.doc: A light infinitely far away. Travels along the entity's world -Z axis; rotate the entity to aim it.
fields: color: color = #ffffff [WB] // Light colour (linear RGB; alpha is ignored).
intensity: f32 = 1.0 [WB] // Illuminance in lux.

schemas.name: Dynamic
schemas.doc: A solver-controlled body; forces, impulses and teleports are explicit commands.
fields: mass: f32 = 1.0 [C] // Mass in kilograms.
linear_damping: f32 = 0.0 [C] // Rate at which linear velocity decays.
angular_damping: f32 = 0.05 [C] // Rate at which angular velocity decays.

schemas.name: Emitter
schemas.doc: A bounded particle emitter: at most 64 particles, spawned at `rate` per second in a hemisphere around the entity's up axis.
fields: rate: f32 = 0.0 [C] // Particles spawned per second. A fraction carries to the next frame.
lifetime: f32 = 1.0 [C] // How long each particle lives, in seconds.
speed: f32 = 1.0 [C] // Initial speed in metres per second.
size: f32 = 0.05 [C] // Billboard size in metres.
gravity: f32 = 0.0 [C] // Downward acceleration in metres per second squared.

schemas.name: Entity
schemas.doc: The fields of an entity or prefab body: a named node with a transform and optional components.
fields: position: vec3 = vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0) [WB] // Position local to the parent, in metres.
rotation: quat = quat.identity() [WB] // Rotation local to the parent.
scale: vec3 = vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) [WB] // Scale local to the parent. Construction-only (and `vec3(1.0)` for dynamic and kinematic bodies) when the entity has a body.
visible: bool = true [WB] // Hides the mesh draw only; the entity's behaviour keeps running.
mesh: mesh [C] // The mesh drawn for this entity: a mesh descriptor (`Box`, `Sphere`, `Plane`) or an asset mesh.
material: material = Unlit {} [C] // The material instance used to draw the mesh. The instance is construction-only; its parameters are writable and bindable. Requires `mesh`.
light: light [C] // A light component (`DirectionalLight`, `PointLight`). Its fields are writable and bindable as their schemas say. Named entities only.
body: body [C] // A physics body (`Static`, `Dynamic`, `Kinematic`). Root entities only; requires `collider`.
collider: collider [C] // A collision shape (`BoxCollider`, `SphereCollider`). Requires `body`.

tag: string [C] // A group name (`"rock"`) that `count_tagged`, `first_tagged`, `nearest_tagged`, `tagged`, `has_tag` and `destroy_tagged` look the entity up by (decision 0150). A string literal of lowercase letters, digits and `_`.

particles: emitter [C] // A particle emitter (decision 0155). Up to 64 particles live at once. They are drawn with this entity's mesh as camera-facing billboards, in the colour of its material. Without a mesh the particles are still counted.
clip: string [C] // The name of a glTF animation that moves this entity (decision 0156). The mesh must be a mesh of that file. It composes with the entity's own transform (decision 0174).

schemas.name: Orthographic
schemas.doc: An orthographic projection (right-handed, clip depth 0 to 1).
fields: height: f32 = 10.0 [WB] // Height of the view volume in world units; the width follows from the aspect ratio.
near: f32 = 0.1 [WB] // Distance to the near plane.
far: f32 = 1000.0 [WB] range > near // Distance to the far plane.

schemas.name: Pbr
schemas.doc: The documented PBR subset (metallic-roughness, no image-based lighting).
fields: base_color: color = #ffffff [WB] // Linear base colour multiplied with the base colour texture.
metallic: f32 = 0.0 [WB] // Metalness; clamped to 0..1 by the lighting model.
roughness: f32 = 0.5 [WB] // Perceptual roughness; clamped to 0.045..1 by the lighting model.
base_color_texture: texture = texture.white() [C] // Base colour texture.
base_color_sampler: sampler = sampler.linear_repeat() [C] // Sampler for the base colour texture.

schemas.name: Perspective
schemas.doc: A perspective projection (right-handed, clip depth 0 to 1).
fields: fov_y: f32 = 0.9 [WB] range (0, π) // Full vertical field of view in radians.
near: f32 = 0.1 [WB] // Distance to the near plane.
far: f32 = 1000.0 [WB] range > near // Distance to the far plane.

schemas.name: Plane
schemas.doc: A single-sided horizontal plane at y = 0 facing +Y.
fields: size: vec2 = vec2(1.0, 1.0) [C] // Extent along X and Z.

schemas.name: PointLight
schemas.doc: A light radiating from the entity's world position.
fields: color: color = #ffffff [WB] // Light colour (linear RGB; alpha is ignored).
intensity: f32 = 1.0 [WB] // Luminous intensity in candela.
range: f32 = 0.0 [C] // Distance at which the light fades to nothing; 0 means unlimited.

schemas.name: Scene
schemas.doc: The fields of a scene declaration. All are construction-only and must be constant expressions.
fields: clear_color: color = #000000 [C] // Colour the canvas is cleared to. Only the RGB channels are used.
ambient_color: color = #ffffff [C] // Colour of the ambient light term of lit materials. Only the RGB channels are used.

ambient_intensity: f32 = 0.0 [C] // Scale of the ambient light term of lit materials; 0 turns ambient light off. Like every lit result it is multiplied by the camera's exposure scale (about 3.14 at the default exposure), so 0.3 already gives nearly full brightness on white. Unlit materials ignore it.
gravity: vec3 = vec3(0.0, -9.81, 0.0) [C] // Gravitational acceleration in metres per second squared. Used only when the scene has physics bodies.

schemas.name: Sphere
schemas.doc: A UV sphere centred on the origin.
fields: radius: f32 = 0.5 [C] // Radius in metres.
segments: u32 = 32 [C] range 3…256 // Subdivisions around the Y axis.
rings: u32 = 16 [C] range 2…256 // Subdivisions from pole to pole.

schemas.name: SphereCollider
fields: radius: f32 [RC] // Radius in metres.
sensor: bool = false [C] // A sensor reports collisions but does not push other bodies.
friction: f32 = 0.5 [C] // Coulomb friction coefficient.
restitution: f32 = 0.0 [C] range 0…1 // Bounciness, 0 (none) to 1 (perfect).

schemas.name: Sprite
schemas.doc: One frame of a sprite sheet, tinted; always translucent.
fields: sheet: texture = texture.white() [C] // The sprite sheet: `columns` x `rows` equal cells.
sheet_sampler: sampler = sampler.nearest_clamp() [C] // Sampler of the sheet (default nearest, clamped: crisp pixels).
tint: color = #ffffff [WB] // Multiplies the texel, alpha included.
cell: f32 = 0.0 [WB] // The cell (animation frame) shown, from 0, left to right then top to bottom; floored and wrapped, so `bind(t * fps)` animates.
columns: f32 = 1.0 [WB] range 1…64 // Cells per row of the sheet.
rows: f32 = 1.0 [WB] range 1…64 // Rows of cells in the sheet.

schemas.name: Unlit
fields: color: color = #ffffff [WB] // The colour written to the canvas.

enums.name: Key
enums.doc: A physical keyboard key, independent of the layout. Written `Key.<Member>` with exactly the members listed (`Key.Space`, `Key.ArrowUp`, `Key.A`, `Key.Digit1`); there is no `Key.Up`, `Key.KeyA` or `Key.Shift`. Maps from the DOM `KeyboardEvent.code`.

hud.text(content: string, at: vec2, [size: f32, tint: color, align: f32, font: font]) -> () [handler] // Draws a line of text at `at` (canvas NDC, y up): `size` in CSS pixels (default 24.0), `tint` (default white), `align` 0.0 puts the left edge at `at`, 0.5 the centre (default), 1.0 the right edge, `font` an `asset.font(..)` or `hud.pixel_font()` (default: the page's sans-serif). The line is centred vertically on `at`.
hud.pixel_font() -> font [handler] // The built-in font: a 5x7 pixel bitmap of printable ASCII, the same in every browser (decision 0139). Other characters show as a box.

hud.rect(at: vec2, size: vec2, tint: color, [align: f32]) -> () [handler] // Draws a filled rectangle of `size` CSS pixels at `at` (canvas NDC), aligned like `hud.text` (default centred). For panels and bars.

hud.button(label: string, at: vec2, [size: f32]) -> bool [handler] // Draws a button centred at `at` (canvas NDC) with the label `label` (`size` in CSS pixels, default 24.0). Returns true in the frame after the button was clicked, once per click; buttons are told apart by their label and their order among buttons with that label.
gamepad.axis(pad: i32, axis: i32) -> f32 [CPU] // Axis in [-1,1]; missing/disconnected is zero.
gamepad.button(pad: i32, button: i32) -> f32 [CPU] // Button pressure in [0,1]; missing/disconnected is zero.
gamepad.connected(pad: i32) -> bool [CPU] // Whether the pad is connected.
easing.in_quad|out_quad|in_out_quad|in_cubic|out_cubic|in_out_cubic|in_out_sine|out_back|out_elastic|out_bounce(t: f32) -> f32 [CPU] // `t` is clamped to 0..1, the result is 0 at 0 and 1 at 1.
lighting.pbr(surface: SurfaceInput, base_color: color, metallic: f32, roughness: f32) -> color [GPU] // The documented PBR subset evaluated for every light in the scene.
screen_to_world(point: vec2, z: f32) -> vec3 [CPU] // Canvas NDC to the world Z plane `z`; parallel rays return NaN x/y.
world_to_screen(point: vec3) -> vec2 [CPU] // World position to canvas NDC, using the active camera and viewport.
overlap_spheres(a: vec3, radius_a: f32, b: vec3, radius_b: f32) -> bool [CPU] // World-space sphere intersection, including touching. No physics required.

overlap_boxes(a: vec3, size_a: vec3, rotation_a: quat, b: vec3, size_b: vec3, rotation_b: quat) -> bool [CPU] // Oriented box intersection; world centers, full sizes and rotations. No physics required.
send(target: entity_ref, message: string) -> () [handler] // Queues a string for a live entity's `on message(value: string)` handler.
sample(t: texture, s: sampler, uv: vec2) -> vec4 [GPU] // Filtered texel of `t` at `uv`. `texture` and `sampler` parameters may be used only as direct arguments to `sample`.
random() -> f32 [CPU] // A pseudo-random number in `[0, 1)`.
random_range(lo: f32, hi: f32) -> f32 [CPU] // A random f32 in `[lo, hi)`.
random_int(lo: i32, hi: i32) -> i32 [CPU] // A random i32 in `[lo, hi)`; `lo` if `hi <= lo`.
chance(p: f32) -> bool [CPU] // True with probability `p`.
choose(items: array<T, N>) -> T [CPU] // One element of an array, chosen uniformly.
shuffle(items: array<T, N>) -> array<T, N> [CPU] // A new array with the same elements in a random order.
print(message: string) -> () [CPU] // Writes a message to the development console.
is_key_down(key: Key) -> bool [CPU] // Whether the key was down at the end of input handling in the current frame.
key_pressed(key: Key) -> bool [CPU] // Whether the key went down during input handling of the current frame.
key_released(key: Key) -> bool [CPU] // Whether the key went up during input handling of the current frame.
pointer_position() -> vec2 [CPU] // The pointer position at the end of input handling, in canvas NDC.
is_pointer_down(button: i32) -> bool [CPU] // Whether pointer button `button` was down at the end of input handling.

spawn(prefab: prefab descriptor) -> entity_ref [handler] // Queues creation of a prefab instance as a root entity; the reference is valid immediately and `alive` turns true after the next lifecycle flush.
destroy(target: entity_ref) -> () [handler] // Queues removal of a spawned entity; it counts as dead from the moment of the call.
play(sound: sound, [volume: f32, pitch: f32]) -> () [handler] // Plays a sound once, at a volume (default 1.0, range 0..4) and a pitch (playback rate, default 1.0, range 0.0625..16).
play_at(sound: sound, position: vec3, [volume: f32]) -> () [handler] // Plays a sound once from a world position: it is quieter further from the active camera and panned left or right.
play_music(sound: sound, [volume: f32]) -> () [handler] // Starts a sound as looping music, replacing the music that plays (one music track at a time).
stop_music|reset|pause|resume|save|clear_saved() -> () [handler]
set_volume(volume: f32) -> () [handler] // Sets the global volume of every sound and the music (default 1.0, range 0..4).
set_muted(muted: bool) -> () [handler] // Mutes or unmutes all audio; the volume is kept.
is_muted|paused() -> bool [CPU]
go_to(scene: scene name) -> () [handler] // Switches scene, keeping shared state.
set_camera(camera: camera name) -> () [handler] // Switches the active camera.
particle_count() -> i32 [CPU] // How many particles are alive.
load() -> bool [handler] // Reads saved values back; false if none.
alive(target: entity_ref) -> bool [CPU] // Whether the entity reference points at a live entity.
count_tagged(tag: string) -> i32 [CPU] // The number of live entities with the tag.
first_tagged(tag: string) -> entity_ref [CPU] // The first live entity with the tag in instance order; a dead reference (`alive` is false) if there is none.
nearest_tagged(tag: string, point: vec3) -> entity_ref [CPU] // The live entity with the tag whose world position is nearest `point`; a dead reference if there is none.
has_tag(target: entity_ref, tag: string) -> bool [CPU] // Whether the entity is live and has the tag.
tagged(tag: string) -> tagged entities [CPU] // The live entities with the tag, in instance order: only the iterable of a `for` loop (`for r in tagged("rock") { .. }`).
destroy_tagged(tag: string) -> () [handler] // Queues removal of every live spawned entity with the tag; the tag must not be one a named entity has.
events: on message(<name>: string) [in entity and prefab] // A queued string sent to this entity; delivered before its next unpaused update.
on key_down(Key.<member>) // Delivered when the filtered key transitions to pressed. Auto-repeat is ignored.
on key_up(Key.<member>) // Delivered when the filtered key is released.
on pointer_down(<name>: PointerEvent) // A pointer button was pressed on the canvas.
on pointer_up(<name>: PointerEvent) // A pointer button was released.
on pointer_move(<name>: PointerEvent) // The pointer moved; at most once per frame with the latest position.
on collision_enter(<name>: entity_ref) [in entity and prefab, needs a collider] // The entity's collider started touching another entity's collider; the parameter is the other entity.
on collision_exit(<name>: entity_ref) [in entity and prefab, needs a collider] // The entity's collider stopped touching another entity's collider; the parameter is the other entity.
records: SurfaceInput { local_position: vec3, world_position: vec3, world_normal: vec3, uv: vec2 } // The interpolated inputs of a material fragment stage.
PointerEvent { position: vec2, button: i32 } // A pointer event: `position` in normalised canvas coordinates (x right, y up, both in -1..1) and the `button` (0 primary, 1 middle, 2 secondary).
body: <Entity>.body.teleport(position: vec3, rotation: quat, keep_velocity: bool) [Dynamic, Kinematic]
<Entity>.body.linear_velocity: vec3 [Dynamic, Kinematic] // Linear velocity as of the last completed tick. Read-only.
<Entity>.body.angular_velocity: vec3 [Dynamic, Kinematic] // Angular velocity as of the last completed tick. Read-only.

notes: color: Linear-light RGBA with straight alpha; distinct from `vec4`. A literal `#rrggbb` is sRGB-encoded and converted; `color.linear(rgb, a)` takes linear components, `color.srgb(rgb, a)` sRGB ones. Fields `.r .g .b .a` and `.rgb`; no arithmetic.

frame: Per-frame values, readable in CPU code and in `bind` expressions, not in GPU stage code (route them through material parameters). `update(dt)` gets the frame delta, which varies from frame to frame; `fixed_update(dt)` runs zero or more times per frame and gets the constant fixed step, 1/60 s by default.

diagnosticsGuide: `mtek check --format json` prints one JSON report; each diagnostic has code, severity, title, message, source (file, startByte, endByte, startLine, startColumn, endLine, endColumn), expected and actual (when relevant), related, notes, suggestedEdits and phase. Fix errors in report order, apply a suggestedEdit only when it is present (they are validated), and never delete the feature a diagnostic is about.
